name: CacheGen (KV cache tensor encoding + bandwidth-adaptive streaming)
bits: adaptive per-part compression level; the paper reports a 3.5-4.3x reduction in KV cache SIZE with negligible response-quality impact
activation_scheme: Not a fixed-bit scheme at all - a custom tensor ENCODER that exploits KV distributional properties to produce a compact bitstream with negligible decoding overhead, with the compression level adapted to available bandwidth (raising compression, or recomputing KV on the fly, when bandwidth drops).
kernels: CacheGen (UChi-JCL/CacheGen) - a context-loading module integrated with a serving system, not a GEMM kernel.
quality_delta: From the abstract: reduces KV cache size by 3.5-4.3x and total delay in fetching and processing contexts by 3.2-3.7x, with negligible impact on LLM response quality, versus systems that reuse the KV cache.
notes:
GROUP SIZE NOT APPLICABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: eviction reduces HOW MANY KV positions are retained; no bits per retained value change, so there is no weight grid to group. The null here is a fact about the method, not missing data. Boundary record, and a genuinely different mechanism from everything else in the KV family. CacheGen targets TRANSFER BANDWIDTH, not GPU capacity: it compresses a cached context so it can be shipped from a remote store quickly, which is the multi-turn and RAG-prefix-reuse case. Compare CacheGen with Pensieve (same problem, GPU/CPU tiering instead of compression) and with KIVI (GPU capacity instead of bandwidth). The adaptive compression level is worth noting: it will raise compression or recompute when bandwidth degrades, so its quality is a function of network conditions at runtime, not a fixed property of the checkpoint. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'bitsandbytes-nf4' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'kv-eviction'. 
NATIVE_SUPPORT CLASSIFIED 2026-10-04: this field is still [] and that is CORRECT, but the empty list used to be ambiguous between three different states and now is not. Reason class on this record: KV-CACHE-ONLY, SO STRUCTURALLY ABSENT. The bits field records that no bits-per-value change: the scheme reduces WHICH positions are retained, fetched or reallocated, so it runs on whatever precision path the accelerator already has for the KV cache. A KV-position policy can never be a hardware format. Consequence for a reader: nothing further to verify - this is a cache-management policy, not a numeric format. The full statement of the three-way distinction, and the worked list of all 72 empty records by class, is in gotcha quant-native-support-empty-means-three-different-things. Rule of thumb for this field everywhere in the repo: if the bits field carries an 'a16', or the scheme is KV-cache-only or a llama.cpp integer storage type, an empty native_support is a DEFINITION and needs no verification; only a W4A4/W8A8/sub-8-bit format with research kernels can have an empty list that is a real finding.
